title: Shape Memory Alloys in Biomedical Engineering: a Scopus-Based Bibliometric Analysis and Research Trajectory Forecasting via Machine Learning
html: Shape memory alloys (SMAs) have emerged as transformative materials in biomedical engineering because of their shape memory effect, superelasticity, and biocompatibility. This study presents a bibliometric analysis of SMA research in biomedical engineering based on 351 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2011 and 2024, integrated with machine learning and transformer-based language models to identify research themes and forecast research trajectories. The field grew at an annual rate of 16.36%, with 30.77% of articles involving international co-authorship. Citation, collaboration and keyword analyses identified the most influential articles, authors, journals, institutions and countries, with the United States leading in both output and citation impact. Burst detection revealed a shift from early work on the shape memory effect, stents, and cardiovascular tissue interactions towards corrosion and surface behavior and, most recently, laser powder bed fusion and titanium-based alloys. Semantic clustering using SPECTER document embeddings, UMAP, and HDBSCAN identified three research themes: cardiovascular stents and devices; sensing and surgical devices; biomaterials and biocompatibility. Prophet forecasting, validated on a 2024 hold-out year, projects continued growth in all three themes through 2030, with the strongest increase in Biomaterials and biocompatibility. The proposed framework provides an overview of the intellectual structure, emerging themes, and future development of SMA research in biomedical engineering, offering insights for researchers, clinicians, and materials scientists.
